ai_evidence: Real Ollama (qwen2.5:1.5b) + MiniLM: acceptance evidence for AI behaviour.

scenarios.title: Document ingestion
scenarios.preconditions: Apex tenant exists with no documents; support engineer signed in
scenarios.test_data: Fictional Apex pump manual (PDF), inspection report (PDF), equipment register, incident history and maintenance log (CSV)
steps: Upload each of the five sample files
Upload the equipment register again unchanged
List the documents
Search for a manual passage and read its provenance
scenarios.expected: Five documents created with chunks; the repeat upload is reported as duplicate; hashes and versions are listed; search results carry page numbers (PDF) or record ids (CSV)
scenarios.actual: 5 documents ingested {'apex_cp200_pump_manual.pdf': ('created', 3), 'apex_inspection_report_2026q3.pdf': ('created', 1), 'equipment_register.csv': ('created', 4), 'incident_history.csv': ('created', 5), 'maintenance_log.csv': ('created', 3)}; repeat upload 'duplicate'; first hit page=None

scenarios.title: Evidence-grounded retrieval
steps: Ask each question
Check every citation: source ownership and verbatim quote
Ask an out-of-scope question
scenarios.expected: Every answer shown is grounded with verified citations from Apex documents; unanswerable questions get an insufficient-evidence response with no citation. For the real model: at least 2 of the 3 prepared questions produce a verified grounded answer (measured Phase 3 coverage was about 75%)
scenarios.actual: 3 of 3 answerable questions grounded with verified citations; out-of-scope question refused

answers.question: What should I check when pump P-101 shows abnormal vibration at the drive-end bearing?
At what vibration velocity should the CP-200 pump be stopped?
What causes cavitation in the pump and what should be done?

scenarios.limitations: Real-model coverage varies between runs; the 95% citation-correctness target remains NOT MET (Phase 3/4).

scenarios.title: Historical incident matching
scenarios.test_data: Report: P-101 abnormal vibration 8.4 mm/s with grinding noise
steps: Extract an incident from the report
Inspect related incidents
scenarios.expected: Past incidents for the same equipment (INC-2024-0412, INC-2025-0107) are listed, same-asset first, from Apex's own history

scenarios.title: Structured ticket generation
scenarios.test_data: Report: P-101 abnormal vibration 8.4 mm/s with grinding noise
steps: Extract the incident
Check the validated fields
Create a ticket draft (after human review if the platform requires it)
scenarios.expected: A schema-valid incident (asset P-101 verified, category, symptoms, priority P2 from deterministic rules, citations or an explicit no-evidence note, review status); a draft whose content carries the asset, priority, evidence and notes
scenarios.actual: incident pending_review (category mechanical_vibration, 1 citation(s)); draft DRAFT
scenarios.limitations: In real-AI mode the model's category and symptoms vary; priority is rule-based.

scenarios.title: Unapproved submission blocked
scenarios.test_data: Two tickets: one PENDING_APPROVAL, one REJECTED
steps: Try to submit an unapproved ticket
Let the worker run
Engineer tries to approve
Supervisor rejects; try to retry/submit the rejected ticket
scenarios.expected: Submission refused (409); the external system receives nothing; engineers cannot approve; a rejected ticket can never be submitted
scenarios.actual: submit before approval 409; engineer approval 403; rejected ticket submit/retry 409; worker idle; mock requests 0

scenarios.title: Approved ticket submission
steps: Request approval
Supervisor approves
Worker submits
Read the ticket and the audit trail
scenarios.expected: The ticket reaches the maintenance mock exactly once, its external id (MNT-) is stored, and the audit trail records draft, approval and submission
scenarios.actual: ticket SUBMITTED as MNT-1006; 1 external ticket; audit has draft, approval, submission

scenarios.title: Duplicate prevention
scenarios.preconditions: Apex incident ready for a ticket
scenarios.test_data: Concurrent drafts, concurrent approvals, direct re-submit, lost-response retry
steps: Create tickets for one incident from 5 threads
Approve one ticket from 6 threads
Re-submit and re-approve
Inject a lost response and let the worker retry
scenarios.expected: One ticket per incident; one approval wins; one external ticket in every case, including after a lost response
scenarios.actual: draft codes [201, 409, 409, 409, 409]; approval codes [200, 409, 409, 409, 409, 409]; worker ['retry_scheduled', 'submitted']; external tickets 1

scenarios.title: API failure recovery
scenarios.preconditions: Apex approved tickets; maintenance mock configurable
scenarios.test_data: Two consecutive HTTP 503 responses; one permanent HTTP 400
steps: Approve a ticket while the mock returns 503 twice
Run the worker
Approve another while the mock returns 400
Fix and retry as a supervisor
scenarios.expected: Transient failures are retried with backoff and end SUBMITTED once; a permanent failure is FAILED (not retried automatically) and a supervisor retry then succeeds with exactly one external ticket per ticket
scenarios.actual: 503 x2: ['retry_scheduled', 'retry_scheduled', 'submitted'], attempts 3; 400: FAILED then supervisor retry SUBMITTED; external tickets 2 for 2 tickets

scenarios.title: Second-tenant onboarding
scenarios.preconditions: Platform running with Apex; Meridian origins authorized by the operator (server allow-list); no Meridian code exists in the services
scenarios.test_data: onboarding/meridian.json (tenant, members, connectors, domain profile, documents)
steps: Run the onboarding tool against the public API only
Read the onboarding health checks
Check that no customer-specific tables exist
scenarios.expected: Meridian exists as a separate tenant with members, connectors, profile and documents created through supported APIs only, and all health checks pass; the database schema contains no Meridian-specific objects
scenarios.actual: 8 of 8 onboarding checks pass; profile v1; no customer-specific tables

scenarios.title: Customer-specific schema mapping
scenarios.preconditions: Meridian onboarded with field mappings in its profile
scenarios.test_data: fleet_register.csv, service_history.csv, telematics_alerts.csv with Meridian's own column names
steps: Search for a service record
Inspect the stored passage and record id
scenarios.expected: Records are keyed by Meridian's ids (VH-xxxx, SR-xxxx) and carry the mapped column names (vehicle_id, root_cause, resolution)
scenarios.actual: service record SR-3002 and register record VH-2101 carry mapped columns

scenarios.title: Fleet issue extraction
scenarios.preconditions: Meridian onboarded; fleet and CRM mocks running
scenarios.test_data: Report: Vehicle VH-2101 shows low brake pressure of 52 psi with a hissing noise at the rear axle.
steps: Extract the incident
Check asset verification, deterministic priority and enrichment notes
Extract a report with no vehicle id
scenarios.expected: VH-2101 identified and verified against the fleet register; priority P2 from Meridian's rules (brake pressure 52 psi); fleet telematics and CRM notes present; a report without a vehicle id is rejected, never guessed
scenarios.actual: VH-2101 verified; category leak; priority P2; 0 citation(s); enrichments present
scenarios.limitations: In real-AI mode the model may choose a near-miss category (observed: 'leak'); priority follows the extracted category and the regex-read signals.

scenarios.title: Ticket approval
steps: Draft and request approval as an engineer
Engineer tries to approve
Supervisor approves
scenarios.expected: The author cannot approve; the supervisor's decision is recorded with a comment; the ticket becomes APPROVED
scenarios.actual: author approval 403; supervisor approval recorded with comment; ticket APPROVED

scenarios.title: Correct customer API submission
scenarios.preconditions: Meridian connector maps to the service-desk work-order contract; Apex also active
scenarios.test_data: Approved Meridian ticket and an approved Apex ticket in the same worker queue
steps: Approve both tickets
Run the worker
Inspect each external system
scenarios.expected: Meridian's ticket arrives only at its service desk as a work order with the mapped fields and urgency (WO- id); Apex's reaches only its own system (MNT- id)
scenarios.actual: work order WO-7004 with mapped fields; Apex system received only its own ticket

scenarios.title: Cross-tenant access denied
scenarios.preconditions: Apex and Meridian both hold incidents, tickets and documents
scenarios.test_data: Apex and Meridian users of every role
steps: Create a ticket in each tenant
Each tenant's users try to read and act on the other's objects
Search and ask from each tenant for the other's content
scenarios.expected: Every cross-tenant read or action is denied or hidden; retrieval never returns the other tenant's passages; audit trails are separate
scenarios.actual: 12 of 12 cross-tenant attempts denied; searches stayed inside each tenant; audit trails separate

scenarios.title: Failure recovery
scenarios.preconditions: Meridian approved tickets; service-desk mock configurable
scenarios.test_data: HTTP 503 once, then a lost response
steps: Approve a ticket while the service desk returns 503
Run the worker
Approve another and lose the response
Run the worker
scenarios.expected: Both tickets end SUBMITTED; each produced exactly one work order (the lost response is replayed with the same idempotency key)
scenarios.actual: 503: ['retry_scheduled', 'submitted']; lost response: ['retry_scheduled', 'submitted']; work orders 2 for 2 tickets
